newsitem.title: UK: North Sea schedules 280,000 bpd Sept supply dip.
newsitem.headline: North Sea schedules 280,000 bpd Sept supply dip.

text.p: British and Norwegian crude liftings from the North Sea's seven main export systems are scheduled to fall by 280,000 barrels in day (bpd) in September, loading programmes released this week show.
September programmes schedule 4.15 million bpd from Brent, Ekofisk, Flotta, Forties, Gullfaks, Oseberg, Statfjord and Troll compared to a revised 4.43 million in August.
Lower exports are expected from Statfjord, where delayed August cargoes have curtailed the September programme, Gullfaks, Brent and Flotta.
Only Oseberg is expected to raise supplies after returning from maintenance in August.
Following are details of the September North Sea crude loading schedules with previous month comparisons:
Note: Five August Statfjord cargoes deferred to early September
Brent and Oseberg are shown measured in 500,000-barrel cargoes. Statfjord and Gullfaks are 855,000 barrels while Ekofisk are mainly 500,000 barrels.
Forties cargoes normally vary between 400,000 to one million barrels. Flotta cargoes are normally 500,000, 600,000 and 650,000 barrels and Troll is normally between 400,000 and one million barrels.
